title: coord keeps an operation job as the key job/ID with a state table of its own, and every move posts a job event
goal: coord.py transition accepts a key job/ID with a table of its own (none to queued; queued to running or cancelled; running to waiting-lock, waiting-merge, succeeded, failed, refused, cancelled or lost; waiting-lock and waiting-merge back to running or on to cancelled; lost to queued or failed; succeeded, failed, refused and cancelled move nowhere), posts a job event of job, state, op, item, exit, step, by and attempt on every move, and a move the table refuses exits 1 naming the state the key holds, while an unknown state exits 2; coord.py wait --kind job returns on such an event; the table of run/ITEM keys is unchanged (queued is no run state, exit 2)

run: import json,subprocess,sys,tempfile,os; s=os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(),"c.sqlite"); co=lambda *a: subprocess.run([sys.executable,"_tools/coord.py","--store",s,*a],capture_output=True,text=True); t=lambda k,to,*f: co("transition",k,"--to",to,*f).returncode; k="job/JB-aaaaaaaa"; assert t(k,"queued")==0 and t(k,"running")==0; assert t(k,"queued")==1; assert t(k,"succeeded","--field","exit=0")==0; assert t(k,"running")==1; assert t(k,"bogus")==2; assert t("run/ST-aaaaaaaa","queued")==2; ev=json.loads(co("wait","--since","0","--timeout","0","--kind","job").stdout)["events"]; assert [e["fields"]["state"] for e in ev]==["queued","running","succeeded"], ev

import json,subprocess,sys,tempfile,os
s=os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(),"c.sqlite"); co=lambda *a: subprocess.run([sys.executable,"_tools/coord.py","--store",s,*a],capture_output=True,text=True)
t=lambda k,to: co("transition",k,"--to",to).returncode
a="job/JB-bbbbbbbb"; assert [t(a,x) for x in ("queued","running","waiting-lock","running","waiting-merge","running","lost","queued","running","lost","failed","queued")]==[0]*11+[1]
b="job/JB-cccccccc"; assert [t(b,x) for x in ("queued","cancelled","running")]==[0,0,1]
e="job/JB-dddddddd"; assert [t(e,x) for x in ("queued","running","waiting-lock","cancelled")]==[0,0,0,0]
ev=json.loads(co("wait","--since","0","--timeout","0","--kind","job").stdout)["events"]; assert ev and all(f in x["fields"] for x in ev for f in ("job","state")), ev

notes: Shape: the value of job/ID is one JSON object (the record kj_store writes at submit: job, op, subject, host, clone, operator, by, options, attempt, submitted_ts, and the members the executor sets: state, exit, step, pid), and transition on a job/ID key rewrites its state, exit and step members and keeps every other, in the same BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction that posts the job event (as run/ITEM does with its state, coord.py:600 transition); the first move none to queued creates {state: queued}, and kj_store's submit gives the other members in that one write, so a job is one key and one event stream. A sibling table beside the run table, not an extension of it: run/ITEM says where an item is in its work (coordination.md:55), job/ID says where an operation is; the job's own step is the CLI's last land.step name. Closed event fields are added where coord.KIND_FIELDS and check_kind (coord.py:549) hold the others; no other file names KIND_FIELDS (referrers: coord.py only). Wait: coord.py wait --kind job --item ID returns on a move (wait, coord.py:690, already filters by kind and item ids of 1 to 120 characters, so JB-... ids fit item_ids). Evidence for why the layer is a table and not new storage: the store is one SQLite file with entries and an append-only events table, writes serialise on BEGIN IMMEDIATE with a 30 s wait (coordination.md:7-9), and every session of a clone, worker worktrees included, already shares it. No test added (ceiling); a planted-store check runs the table.
